t: #3153 Sum of Digit Differences of All Pairs
o: **Understanding the problem**: All numbers share the same digit count d. The digit difference of a pair counts mismatched positions. Summing over all C(n,2) pairs naively is O(n²d) — too slow for n = 10⁵. Instead, work position by position: at a fixed position, pairs agreeing contribute 0; pairs disagreeing contribute 1. With cnt[v] numbers having digit v there, disagreements = C(n,2) − Σ C(cnt[v],2). Example 1: units digits {3,3,2}: C(3,2)−(1+1)=1; tens {1,2,1}: 3−1=2; total 3? Recompute: units mismatches = pairs (13,12),(23,12) = 2 → C(3,2)−C(2,2)−C(1,2) = 3−1 = 2; tens mismatches = (13,23),(23,12) = 2 → 3−1 = 2; total 4 ✓.
k: Contribution decomposes independently per digit position.
At one position: disagreements = C(n,2) − Σ_v C(cnt_v, 2) — count equal-digit pairs and subtract from all pairs.

a.n: Approach 1: Per-position frequency counting (single natural approach)
a.i: Extract digits position by position, bucket-count each digit value, and apply the complement formula. Total work O(n·d) with d ≤ 10.
s: Copy nums to avoid mutation; while any number remains nonzero:
Bucket-count the current last digit of every number, then strip that digit.
Add C(n,2) − Σ C(bucket,2) to the answer.
a.t: O(n·d) — d ≤ 10 digit passes over the array
a.sp: O(n) — the mutable digit-stripping copy (O(10) buckets)

a.i: Convert every number to a string once, then for each character index tally digit frequencies — same math, often clearer and avoids repeated division.
s: Convert all numbers to equal-length strings.
For each index, count digit frequencies across all strings.
Accumulate C(n,2) − Σ C(cnt,2) per index.
a.t: O(n·d) — one string conversion pass plus d counting passes
a.sp: O(n·d) — stored strings (vs O(n) for the division variant)

w: **Wrap-up**: The complement trick (total pairs minus agreeing pairs) is the whole problem — state it early. Pitfalls: 64-bit accumulation (pairs reach ~5·10⁹), and stopping the digit loop correctly (all numbers share digit count, so looping while vals[0] > 0 is safe). Follow-ups: sum of digit *similarities*, or answer queries over subranges (prefix count matrices per digit position).
